items.title: De Pedys, ‘The Mediterranean: A Crossroads of Digital Data; Defending It Means Cybersecurity’
items.description: (ANSA) - NAPOLI, 19 NOV - “The Mediterranean dimension is important because more than 95% of data now travels through undersea cables, and the Mediterranean is the crossroads for this data. If you look at the geography, you’ll see that almost all communications between Asia and Europe currently pass through the cables laid in the Red Sea—whether they exit in Egypt or return to the Mediterranean—making it an absolutely crucial point: for this reason, the defense, management, and monitoring of this infrastructure constitute cyber defense in every sense of the word.” Alessandro De Pedys, Director
items.titleIt: De Pedys, ‘The Mediterranean: A Crossroads of Digital Data; Defending It Means Cybersecurity’

items.title: Hassan Sheikh Knew About the UAE for Years. Now It Is Useful
items.description: On Tuesday, 17 November, the president of Somalia went on television and, as I heard it in Somali, said that a brother does not burn your house. items.description: The closure of the U.N. Transitional Assistance Mission in Somalia (UNTMIS) follows a two-year transition agreed with the federal government. items.title: Eritrea: U.S. Lawmaker Proposes Trade Incentives to Push Ethiopia, Eritrea Off Conflict Cliff, Toward Peace
items.description: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- US Republican Representative Jim Baird has proposed two pieces of legislation seeking to link expanded trade and economic cooperation with Ethiopia and Eritrea to progress toward lasting peace, as tensions between the neighboring countries continue to raise fears of a renewed interstate conflict.
items.titleIt: Eritrea: U.S. Lawmaker Proposes Trade Incentives to Push Ethiopia, Eritrea Off Conflict Cliff, Toward Peace

items.title: Sudan: Sudan Drone Strikes 'Acts of Genocide' - Women's Rights Group
items.description: [Dabanga] Amsterdam -- Sudanese women's rights group The No to Oppression against Women Initiative has condemned the continuation of the war in Sudan and the escalating use of drones against civilian-populated areas, including hospitals, schools, and electricity and water facilities, describing the attacks as "acts of genocide" against the Sudanese people.
items.titleIt: Sudan: Sudan Drone Strikes 'Acts of Genocide' - Women's Rights Group

items.title: De Pedys, ‘The Mediterranean: A Crossroads of Digital Data; Defending It Means Cybersecurity’
items.description: (ANSA) - NAPOLI, 19 NOV - “The Mediterranean dimension is important because more than 95% of data now travels through undersea cables, and the Mediterranean is the crossroads for this data. If you look at the geography, you’ll see that almost all communications between Asia and Europe currently pass through the cables laid in the Red Sea—whether they exit in Egypt or return to the Mediterranean—making it an absolutely crucial point: for this reason, the defense, management, and monitoring of this infrastructure constitute cyber defense in every sense of the word.” Alessandro De Pedys, Director
items.titleIt: De Pedys, ‘The Mediterranean: A Crossroads of Digital Data; Defending It Means Cybersecurity’

items.title: Somalia's Eritrean-trained naval chief appointment risks further straining ties with Ethiopia
items.description: Mohamed Abdulqadir "Shariif" has been appointed commander of the Somali Navy and Coastal Defence Forces, replacing Brig. Gen. Abdiwahab Omar. His military training in Eritrea comes at a sensitive time for the region, with relations between Ethiopia and Eritrea deteriorating and renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia raising fears of a wider confrontation.  The appointment could cause concern in Addis Ababa, particularly as Somalia has strengthened its engagement with Eritrea and Egypt amid longstanding disputes with Ethiopia over sovereignty, regional security and access to the Red Sea.
